criteria.name: immutable-source-and-package-identity
criteria.requirement: Every consumed handoff, export, archive, source receipt, and declared package identity is hash-bound and read back from the artifact; rejected or revoked identities remain hard failures.

criteria.name: package-metadata-ownership-and-closure
criteria.requirement: PKGINFO, MTREE, dependencies, conflicts, file ownership, case-insensitive collisions, licenses, and documentation are truthful and complete; no fake provides, aliases, or ownership claims are permitted.

criteria.name: target-architecture-and-import-closure
criteria.requirement: Shipped native files have the required ARM64 machine identity and every DLL or executable import is resolved by an allowed package or system DLL for that artifact's own runtime contract.

criteria.name: private-path-and-relocation-hygiene
criteria.requirement: Payloads, metadata, static archives, and compiled operational strings contain no prohibited producer-private roots; moved-root behavior and package-time relocation are proven without altering unrelated payload bytes.

criteria.name: functional-and-upstream-evidence
criteria.requirement: The provider supplies preserved build, test, and moved-root consumer evidence appropriate to its claimed scope; missing, skipped, expected-failure, or harness-limited coverage is recorded rather than promoted to a pass.

criteria.name: runtime-cohort-and-role-separation
criteria.requirement: MINGWARM64/UCRT, native MSYS runtime cohorts, managed components, shipped-native payload, self-hosting evidence, and SDK/header-only inputs remain separate gates; evidence for one role or cohort cannot be inferred for another.

criteria.name: complete-contract-and-release-gate
criteria.requirement: All contract-required Git splits, packages, files, documentation, licenses, launch paths, managed admissions, native self-hosting evidence, TLS selection, and dependency closure must pass before a release archive is emitted; an incomplete audit remains incomplete.

standingRules: Limited libintl and PCRE2 byte projections do not satisfy strict GNU package identity or transaction gates.
A valid provider admission may be unselected by the current full-release contract.
No runtime-907 admission implies d70 compatibility, and no d70 admission implies runtime-907 compatibility.
MinGW/UCRT libraries must not be forced to import msys-2.0.dll; genuine MSYS providers and consumers must prove their exact MSYS runtime cohort.
Missing input is not proof that a component was never built, but it cannot be consumed until an exact qualified handoff is supplied.
No complete archive may be emitted while any blocker remains.
